Simulated individual salamander genotypes and resistance analyses

Source: R/individual_salamanders_data.R
individual_salamanders.Rd

Matched SNP and microsatellite genotypes for 160 adult terrestrial salamanders in each of two simulated movement scenarios on a real southeastern Ohio landscape. The primary example demonstrates nonlinear isolation by resistance with individual sampling. The animals and drying index are hypothetical; neither species occurrence nor field-calibrated movement is claimed.

Usage

data(individual_salamanders)

Format

A list with three elements:

data

Two named scenarios, compensatory_500 and control_500. Each contains samples, snp_dosage, microsat_alleles, and covariance, described below.

models

Twenty checked model records per scenario: uniform and quadratic drying models, two marker types, and partitions 0 (all adults) through 4 (one spatial quadrant withheld). Names combine marker, model, and partition, for example SNP2500__IBR__0. Records contain log-conductance coefficients theta, graph covariance multiplier phi$tau on its natural nonnegative scale, log nugget variance phi$sigma, starting-point diagnostics, convergence, curvature, covariance score, RMSE, and predicted-mean range. These are plain lists, not fitted terradish objects.

metadata

Fixed drying center center, linear divisor sd_linear, and quadratic divisor sd_quadratic; the latter is SD of squared deviations, not squared SD. start_halfwidth defines additional starting points, not coefficient bounds. epsg, native_resolution_m, graph_resolution_m, directions, extent, core, and graph_nodes describe the spatial grid (EPSG:26917, meters). sample_size, main_SNPs, and matched_microsatellites give panel sizes. objective, biological_scope, and raw_marker_selection state interpretation and selection rules.

Source

Simulated genotypes from recorded individual pedigrees on terrain derived from USGS 3DEP elevation and 2023 Annual NLCD Collection 1.0. See system.file("extdata", "individual-salamanders", "README.md", package = "terradish") for data sources, processing, and limitations.

Details

Within each scenario, samples has 160 rows in genotype order. sample_id and sample_key identify the animal; id, mom, and dad are recorded ecological pedigree identifiers. stratum gives one of 16 sampling strata; quadrant and fold identify the four spatial validation blocks. age is in years, sex is 0 for female and 1 for male, x_local and y_local are meters from the domain origin, and easting and northing are projected UTM coordinates. drying is the interpolated hypothetical index from 0 to 1.

snp_dosage contains nested integer matrices named 500, 1000, and 2500. Entries 0, 1, and 2 count one allele. Locus names identify synthetic genomic blocks and within-block positions. microsat_alleles is a 160 by 48 integer matrix; adjacent columns hold the two repeat-count alleles at each of 24 loci. All marker row names match samples$sample_id. Microsatellite allele labels are categorical, not continuous response values.

covariance contains centered matrices named SNP2500 and microsat24, averaging unstandardized allele-frequency inner products across loci. Their implied squared distances range from 0 to 2. This is different from the locus-frequency weighting in cov_from_biallelic and is not a Dps response.

Each scenario follows 500 years, with maximum age 20 for both sexes. The compensatory scenario allows faster, straighter movement at intermediate drying but greater danger in very dry terrain. The control holds behavioral drying at 0.5 while retaining forest settlement and demography. It is a control for drying-dependent movement, not every possible resistance effect. Samples occupy distinct 10 m cells, are at least 10 m apart, and exclude direct or shared recorded parents and grandparents. Distant kin can remain.

These analyses use wishart_covariance with nu = 1 as a covariance quasi-likelihood, not a literal independent-Gaussian-locus sampling model. Nominal Hessian uncertainty, AIC, and significance tests are not used as genetic-sampling evidence. Two hundred genomic-block resamples and a second genomic assay check conditional marker variation; neither supplies independent ecological replication. Spatial folds were reused during workflow development. Marker discovery conditions on the full sampled panel. The matched microsatellites retain mixed predictive evidence. No separate causal isolation-by-environment effect was simulated.

Installed files in extdata/individual-salamanders provide the 10 m drying terms and environment, native 30 m terrain, all 40 original prediction records, comparative scores, the independent assay, and provenance. The 10 m grid interpolates native 30 m information; it adds no new measurements. The vignette explains these files and the longer opt-in reproduction.

Worked examples

vignette("v12-data-generation", package = "terradish"), vignette("v09-individual-salamanders", package = "terradish").

See also

cov_from_genetic_data, cov_from_biallelic, dist_from_cov, vignette("v09-individual-salamanders", package = "terradish").

Other datasets: melip, ohio_ponds

Examples

data(individual_salamanders)
animals <- individual_salamanders$data$compensatory_500
G <- animals$snp_dosage[["2500"]]
S <- cov_from_genetic_data(G, scale = FALSE, normalize = "none") /
  (2 * ncol(G))
dim(S)                              # 160 individual sampling locations
#> [1] 160 160
range(as.matrix(dist_from_cov(S)))   # squared allele-frequency distance
#> [1] 0.000 0.582
table(animals$samples$fold)           # 40 withheld adults per spatial fold
#> 
#>  1  2  3  4 
#> 40 40 40 40
